transcript.content: Hi, welcome in — I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I came in because most days I just wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It's... it's hard to explain, but it feels like the old Ruben, the guy who could talk to anybody and actually enjoy his day, is just gone.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been going on for a couple of weeks, or has it been more of an ongoing thing for months or years?

It's been going on for a while now. I'd say... about eight months. Yeah, right around the time this new regional manager came in. He started really coming down on me, you know? Taking away these accounts that I've handled for years. It's just been a steady downhill since then.
Have you ever had a period—lasting several days or more—where you felt unusually energetic, elated, or needed much less sleep than usual, even if it wasn't during this current low period?

No... no, I can't say I have. I've never really been the type to bounce off the walls or anything. I mean, I used to have normal energy to do my job and talk to my clients, but I always needed my sleep. I haven't ever felt unusually high or energetic like that.

Aside from work, have you also lost interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy—like time with family, hobbies, or other activities—or does the low feeling seem tied mainly to the situation at work?

It's... it's everything, really. Not just work. I used to look forward to things, you know? Like bowling on Thursdays, or working out in the garden... taking my wife to those gallery shows she likes, or even just going dancing. But now, I just sit there. I end up making excuses not to go because... well, none of it even feels worth the effort anymore. I just don't care about doing any of it.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—such as trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty bad lately. At night, I just... I lie there replaying everything from work in my head, just staring at the ceiling. And when I finally do manage to get to sleep, it doesn't last. I usually wake up around three or four in the morning. And I can't get back to sleep after that. I just lie there, already worn out, just dreading having to face the day.
Have you been having any thoughts that you're worthless or excessively guilty, or any thoughts about death or that life isn't worth living?

Yeah, I have. I just keep telling myself that I'm useless now. It feels like... like all those years of taking care of my clients and providing for my family just don't count anymore, all because I can't even handle this job right now. It's hard not to feel guilty about that. I haven't had any thoughts about dying or anything like that, but... yeah, I definitely feel like I'm just worthless to everyone right now.
Right now, are you still able to go to work and manage your daily responsibilities, or has this made it very difficult or impossible for you to function in your usual roles?

It's... it's gotten really difficult. I'm not managing things well at all. At work, I actually just missed a really important client presentation. I just couldn't bring myself to do it. And at home... well, I've pulled back so much there, too. I'm not doing my part with anything. Honestly, that's why I'm here. My wife felt like she had to bring me in today because she said I just wasn't safe carrying on like this.

Right now, are you still able to go into work and handle at least some of your daily tasks, even if with great difficulty, or have you found yourself essentially unable to carry out these responsibilities at all?

Like I was just saying, it's... it's beyond just being difficult at this point. I'm really not handling things at all. I mean, missing that client presentation... that's a big deal in my line of work. I just couldn't do it. And at home, I'm basically useless. I've stopped doing pretty much everything I'm supposed to do. It got to the point where my wife actually brought me in here today. She told me she didn't think I was safe just... continuing on the way I have been.

You mentioned your wife felt you weren't safe continuing on this way—can you tell me more about what led her to feel that, and whether you've had any thoughts, even passing ones, about wishing you were dead or not wanting to wake up?

Well, earlier I said I hadn't had thoughts about dying, but... I guess that wasn't entirely true. I just didn't want to say it out loud. Lately, I've been having these thoughts that maybe my wife and kids would just be better off if I didn't wake up at all. It's like I'm just a burden to them now. And honestly, those thoughts... they scare me. I told my wife about it, and I think that's what really worried her. I just don't trust myself the way I used to, you know? It's getting harder to push those thoughts away.

latest_inference.note: Confirmed passive suicidal ideation (thoughts that family would be better off without him) alongside pervasive anhedonia, worthlessness/guilt, insomnia with early waking, and severe functional impairment (missed work, withdrawal at home) - meeting full criteria for a severe depressive episode without psychotic features.
